title: Capacity-Window Admission & Kernel Handover for Tail Latency Smoothing
creator: Morgan Lee
description: Background: We see intermittent 95-99th percentile latency spikes under mixed workload traffic when small, latency-sensitive requests collide with large-batch throughput waves. Current admission logic admits by token budget and simple age buckets which leads to bursty kernel switching and KV cache churn. This ticket implements a new "capacity window" admission layer combined with a probabilistic kernel handover mechanism to smooth tail behavior while preserving throughput.
proposal: Introduce a capacity-window admission controller that: 1) maintains a short sliding capacity budget per worker (window in ms) that represents CPU/GPU kernel time available for low-latency slots; 2) soft-reserves a tiny slot quota for latency-sensitive requests (soft-slots) and reconciles with overall batch formation; 3) employs a kernel handover budget that lets the runtime decide to keep a prefilling request on the current kernel vs. migrate to a cheaper quantized kernel mid-decode when that reduces expected completion time. The handover decision uses a cheap learned latency model (lightweight ensemble of linear features: current seq len, KV cache hit probability, kernel throughput profile) and a randomized fuse to avoid synchronized handovers across workers.
technical_notes:
- Capacity window is implemented as a per-worker token bucket measured in ms of GPU time, decayed every 50ms.
- Soft-slot reservation: requests marked 'latency' in header get entropy-weighted admission into the soft-slot. If soft-slot quota exhausted, admission is delayed up to a soft deadline (configurable).
- Kernel handover: add 'handover-v2' hint in kernel scheduler; handover cost evaluated via estimator E = decode_remaining_tokens / kernel_throughput - migration_overhead. If E > threshold, trigger migration. Threshold tuned from perf tests.
- Attention opt interactions: when migrating to a quantized kernel, apply attention-window trimming heuristics (shrinking local attention window for non-critical layers) to keep memory bounded. This must be reversible on post-handover decodes.
- Prefill/decode scheduling: prefill admission gives priority weighting to requests with high cache hit probability to maximize prefix reuse across the capacity window.
- Observability: emit events: capacity_window_state, soft_slot_alloc, handover_decision, handover_outcome with sample rate 1/1000 for production to keep telemetry costs low.
metrics_and_targets: Primary targets: reduce 99th percentile decode latency by 20% for mixed traffic (latency+throughput), keep median throughput within 5% of baseline. SLO: <10% request rejection due to soft-slot expiry; no regression on token/sec for heavy batches. Key metrics: decode_latency_p99, kernel_switch_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio, throughput_tokens_per_sec.
acceptance_criteria: A/B test (10% traffic) shows >= 15% p99 improvement and no >5% regression in median throughput over 48h
Kernel switch rate drop by >= 25% in mixed workloads (measured by kernel_switch_rate metric)
No increase in tail error rate (model outputs unchanged within eval tolerances) for customer-critical prompts
Telemetry events show stable capacity_window tokens and handover decisions logged for >95% of decisions
rollout_plan: Canary 5% in us-west-2 for internal customers for 24h
If stable, extend to 25% and run 48h A/B with control group, collect perf and quality signals
Full rollout to hosted and dedicated pools in runtime-1.20 if metrics pass
tests: Synthetic mixed workload harness: latency-small requests (avg 32 tokens) + throughput batches (avg 1024 tokens) at 2:1 ratio
Microbench for handover estimator accuracy using recorded traces (use perf-playback infra)
Integration tests for attention-window trimming to verify reversibility and no state corruption
Chaos test: inject handover-migration delays to validate fallback path
monitoring_and_alerts: alerts: decode_latency_p99 > baseline * 1.25 for 10m -> page on-call SRE
alert: kernel_switch_rate increases > 2x baseline -> rollback flag
daily perf report from A/B job summarizing p50/p95/p99 and throughput deltas
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: synchronized handovers causing transient throughput drop. Mitigation: randomized fuse and staggered handover backoff per worker.
Risk: attention trimming degrading output quality. Mitigation: limit trimming to non-critical layers and run prompt-set evals before rollout.
Risk: telemetry overhead. Mitigation: sample events and use aggregated counters for high-cardinality labels.
